newsitem.title: EAST TIMOR: Timorese bishop denies "scabby dogs" report.
newsitem.headline: Timorese bishop denies "scabby dogs" report.

text.p: East Timorese Bishop Carlos Belo held a news conference to deny comments attributed to him in a German magazine as youths in the troubled Indonesian-ruled territory staged a brief protest outside.
About 500 youths waving banners and shouting "Free East Timor", gathered outside the headquarters of the Nobel peace laureate while he addressed the news conference, witnesses said.
There were no signs of police and the demonstrators dispersed within about an hour, they said.

Inside the office, Belo repeated that he was misquoted in an article published in the German Der Spiegel magazine, in which he was quoted as saying that Indonesian soldiers treated East Timorese like "scabby dogs" and "slaves".
"I hereby state that my interview has been heavily manipulated and seriously distorted," Belo said.
"The expression 'scabby dog' is totally unknown to me. I myself did not know the meaning of the word 'scabby' in English. I came to know of the word only after reading it in Der Spiegel."
The magazine's correspondent has said he stands by his report.
But one of the protesters outside said: "The soldiers treat us badly. Everything the bishop said in Der Spiegel is true."
Indonesia, which is mainly Moslem, invaded predominantly Roman Catholic East Timor in 1975 and annexed it a year later in an act which has not been recognised by the United Nations.
Sporadic resistance to Jakarta's rule still erupts in the territory and some 200 guerrillas are said to be still holed up in the rugged hills of the interior.
Indonesia maintains a large military presence in East Timor compared to its neighbouring provinces, saying that the troops are needed to help development of the territory.
The troubles in East Timor have grabbed world attention since Belo and self-exiled resistance leader Jose Ramos-Horta were jointly awarded the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize last month.
Belo, a popular figure in the territory due to his strong stand on human rights, has strived to walk a tightrope between his disgruntled flock and Indonesian authorities.
